# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# v18: action space + masking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_action_space_size_is_17() -> None:
    """v18 expanded discrete action space from 15 (Phase 6) to 17 (Phase 6 + qi)."""
    from murimsim.actions import N_ACTIONS_PHASE6_QI
    env = _make_combat_env()
    env.reset(seed=0)
    assert env.action_space.n == 17 == N_ACTIONS_PHASE6_QI


def test_mask_gates_attack_qi_when_no_qi() -> None:
    """ATTACK_QI must be masked when attacker has 0 qi, even with adjacent target."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2)
    env._global_step_count = 1_000_000  # past curriculum ramp
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal = env._agents[env._focal_idx]
    other = env._agents[1 - env._focal_idx]
    focal.position = (5, 5)
    other.position = (5, 6)  # adjacent
    focal.inventory.qi = 0
    focal.inventory.food = 0  # avoid eat-mask interference

    mask = env.action_masks()
    assert not mask[Action.ATTACK_QI],    "ATTACK_QI should be masked when qi=0"
    assert not mask[Action.ATTACK_BURST], "ATTACK_BURST should be masked when qi<3"
    assert mask[Action.ATTACK],           "Basic ATTACK should still be available"


def test_mask_gates_attack_burst_when_qi_insufficient() -> None:
    """ATTACK_BURST requires 3 qi; ATTACK_QI requires 1. With 2 qi: only QI available."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2)
    env._global_step_count = 1_000_000
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal = env._agents[env._focal_idx]
    other = env._agents[1 - env._focal_idx]
    focal.position = (5, 5)
    other.position = (5, 6)
    focal.inventory.qi = 2
    focal.inventory.food = 0

    mask = env.action_masks()
    assert mask[Action.ATTACK]
    assert mask[Action.ATTACK_QI],        "ATTACK_QI should be available with qi=2"
    assert not mask[Action.ATTACK_BURST], "ATTACK_BURST should be masked with qi=2 (<3)"


def test_mask_gates_all_attacks_when_no_target() -> None:
    """All ATTACK_* tiers masked when no adjacent agent or monster, regardless of qi."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2)
    env._global_step_count = 1_000_000
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal = env._agents[env._focal_idx]
    other = env._agents[1 - env._focal_idx]
    focal.position = (0, 0)
    other.position = (10, 10)  # far away
    # Move boss away too
    if env._monsters._monsters:
        env._monsters._monsters[0].position = (15, 15)
    focal.inventory.qi = 10  # plenty of qi

    mask = env.action_masks()
    assert not mask[Action.ATTACK]
    assert not mask[Action.ATTACK_QI]
    assert not mask[Action.ATTACK_BURST]


def test_curriculum_gates_all_attack_tiers() -> None:
    """When combat_prob ramp is incomplete, ALL three attack tiers must be gated together."""
    # Use a long ramp and an early step count → combat_prob < 1.0 → some rolls fall through
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2, ramp_steps=1_000_000)
    env._global_step_count = 0  # very early → combat_prob = CURRICULUM_START_PROB (~0.05)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal = env._agents[env._focal_idx]
    focal.inventory.qi = 10
    focal.inventory.food = 0

    # Sample many masks — at least one should have all attacks masked together
    saw_all_three_masked = False
    for _ in range(200):
        mask = env.action_masks()
        if not mask[Action.ATTACK] and not mask[Action.ATTACK_QI] and not mask[Action.ATTACK_BURST]:
            saw_all_three_masked = True
            break
    assert saw_all_three_masked, "Curriculum should occasionally gate all three attack tiers in lockstep"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# v18: end-to-end behavioral tests via env.step
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _setup_focal_vs_boss(qi: int, focal_strength: float = 0.5) -> tuple[CombatEnv, Agent]:
    """Place focal adjacent to the boss with controlled qi + strength. Returns (env, focal)."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=10)
    env._global_step_count = 1_000_000  # past curriculum ramp
    env.reset(seed=42)
    # Need an env with the boss enabled. _make_combat_env doesn't pass enable_boss.
    # Force-spawn a boss for this test.
    if not env._monsters._monsters:
        env._monsters.spawn_boss((0, 0))
    focal = env._agents[env._focal_idx]
    focal.position = (5, 5)
    focal.strength = focal_strength
    focal.inventory.qi = qi
    focal.inventory.food = 5  # avoid critical-eat redirect
    focal.health = 1.0
    env._monsters._monsters[0].position = (5, 6)  # adjacent to focal
    return env, focal


def test_env_step_attack_qi_consumes_one_qi_and_damages_boss() -> None:
    """End-to-end: env.step(ATTACK_QI) deducts 1 qi, damages boss, increments telemetry."""
    env, focal = _setup_focal_vs_boss(qi=5, focal_strength=0.5)
    boss = env._monsters._monsters[0]
    boss_hp_before = boss.health
    qi_before = focal.inventory.qi

    env.step(Action.ATTACK_QI.value)

    assert focal.inventory.qi == qi_before - 1, f"Expected qi {qi_before-1}, got {focal.inventory.qi}"
    assert boss.health < boss_hp_before, f"Boss HP did not drop: before={boss_hp_before}, after={boss.health}"
    assert env._ep_qi_strikes_used == 1
    assert env._ep_qi_spent_in_combat == 1
    assert env._ep_burst_strikes_used == 0


def test_env_step_attack_burst_consumes_three_qi() -> None:
    """End-to-end: env.step(ATTACK_BURST) deducts 3 qi when affordable."""
    env, focal = _setup_focal_vs_boss(qi=5, focal_strength=0.5)
    qi_before = focal.inventory.qi

    env.step(Action.ATTACK_BURST.value)

    assert focal.inventory.qi == qi_before - 3
    assert env._ep_burst_strikes_used == 1
    assert env._ep_qi_spent_in_combat == 3


def test_env_step_attack_burst_downgrades_to_qi_when_insufficient() -> None:
    """env.step(ATTACK_BURST) with 2 qi: downgrades to QI (spends 1, NOT 0)."""
    env, focal = _setup_focal_vs_boss(qi=2, focal_strength=0.5)

    env.step(Action.ATTACK_BURST.value)

    assert focal.inventory.qi == 1, f"Should downgrade BURST→QI, leaving 1 qi; got {focal.inventory.qi}"
    assert env._ep_qi_strikes_used == 1
    assert env._ep_burst_strikes_used == 0


def test_qi_not_consumed_on_whiff() -> None:
    """If ATTACK_QI hits no target (no adjacent monster/agent), qi must NOT be consumed.

    Critical: a misfired strike silently draining the resource pool would teach
    the policy to avoid ATTACK_QI even when it's the right move.
    """
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2)
    env._global_step_count = 1_000_000
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal = env._agents[env._focal_idx]
    other = env._agents[1 - env._focal_idx]
    focal.position = (0, 0)
    other.position = (10, 10)  # far
    if env._monsters._monsters:
        env._monsters._monsters[0].position = (15, 15)  # far
    focal.inventory.qi = 5
    focal.inventory.food = 5

    env.step(Action.ATTACK_QI.value)

    assert focal.inventory.qi == 5, f"Whiffed ATTACK_QI should not consume qi; got {focal.inventory.qi}"
    assert env._ep_qi_strikes_used == 0
    assert env._ep_qi_spent_in_combat == 0


def test_telemetry_surfaces_in_info_at_episode_end() -> None:
    """Per-episode qi-strike counters must appear in info dict on terminal step."""
    env, focal = _setup_focal_vs_boss(qi=4, focal_strength=0.5)
    env.step(Action.ATTACK_QI.value)
    env.step(Action.ATTACK_BURST.value)

    # Force episode termination by killing focal
    focal.health = 0.0
    focal.alive = False
    # One more step to trigger terminal info
    obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(Action.REST.value)

    assert "ep_qi_strikes_used" in info, f"Missing ep_qi_strikes_used in info: keys={list(info.keys())}"
    assert "ep_burst_strikes_used" in info
    assert "ep_qi_spent_in_combat" in info
    assert info["ep_qi_strikes_used"] == 1
    assert info["ep_burst_strikes_used"] == 1
    assert info["ep_qi_spent_in_combat"] == 4


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# v18: damage clamping + DEFEND interaction with high-tier strikes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_burst_damage_respects_max_damage_clamp() -> None:
    """Even at strength=1.0, BURST damage is clamped to COMBAT_MAX_DAMAGE."""
    env = _make_combat_env()
    env.reset(seed=0)
    attacker = _make_agent(strength=1.0)
    defender = _make_agent(strength=0.5)

    dmg_burst = env._combat_damage(attacker, defender, is_defending=False, tier=STRIKE_BURST)
    expected_uncapped = (1.0 + STRIKE_BURST.bonus) * COMBAT_ATTACKER_SCALE  # (1 + 0.7) * 0.5 = 0.85
    assert dmg_burst <= COMBAT_MAX_DAMAGE, f"Burst {dmg_burst} exceeds clamp {COMBAT_MAX_DAMAGE}"
    assert abs(dmg_burst - min(expected_uncapped, COMBAT_MAX_DAMAGE)) < 1e-6


def test_defend_reduces_burst_damage_multiplicatively() -> None:
    """DEFEND's multiplicative reduction must apply AFTER tier bonus, not before."""
    env = _make_combat_env()
    env.reset(seed=0)
    attacker = _make_agent(strength=0.8)
    defender = _make_agent(strength=0.5)

    burst_open    = env._combat_damage(attacker, defender, is_defending=False, tier=STRIKE_BURST)
    burst_blocked = env._combat_damage(attacker, defender, is_defending=True,  tier=STRIKE_BURST)
    assert burst_blocked < burst_open, f"DEFEND must reduce burst dmg: open={burst_open}, blocked={burst_blocked}"
    expected = burst_open * max(0.0, 1.0 - defender.defense_power)
    assert abs(burst_blocked - expected) < 1e-6

def test_combat_focus_fallback_prefers_burst_when_qi_rich() -> None:
    """When in-combat fallback fires AND attacker has 3+ qi, return ATTACK_BURST."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    agent = env._agents[env._focal_idx]
    other = env._agents[1 - env._focal_idx]
    agent.position = (5, 5)
    other.position = (5, 6)  # adjacent target
    agent.inventory.food = 5  # avoid critical-eat path
    agent.inventory.qi = 5
    agent.health = 1.0

    fallback = env._combat_focus_fallback(agent)
    assert fallback == Action.ATTACK_BURST, f"Expected ATTACK_BURST with qi=5, got {fallback.name}"


def test_combat_focus_fallback_uses_qi_when_2_qi() -> None:
    """qi=2 → can't afford BURST(3), should pick ATTACK_QI(1)."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2)
    env.reset(seed=0)

def test_combat_focus_fallback_falls_back_to_basic_when_no_qi() -> None:
    """qi=0 → must return basic ATTACK."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=2)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    agent = env._agents[env._focal_idx]

    agent.position = (5, 5)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# v18: heuristic (non-focal) agents auto-spend qi against boss
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_heuristic_agent_spends_qi_attacking_boss() -> None:
    """Non-focal agent adjacent to boss with qi should auto-spend 1 qi via STRIKE_QI."""
    env = _make_combat_env(n_agents=10)
    env._global_step_count = 1_000_000
    env.reset(seed=42)
    if not env._monsters._monsters:
        env._monsters.spawn_boss((0, 0))
    boss = env._monsters._monsters[0]
    boss.position = (5, 5)

    # Pick a non-focal agent and put them adjacent to boss with qi
    non_focal_idx = (env._focal_idx + 1) % env._n_agents
    helper = env._agents[non_focal_idx]
    helper.position = (5, 6)  # adjacent
    helper.inventory.qi = 3
    helper.inventory.food = 5
    helper.alive = True
    helper.health = 1.0
    helper.strength = 0.5

    qi_before = helper.inventory.qi
    boss_hp_before = boss.health
    # Trigger any focal action — the per-step heuristic loop processes non-focal agents
    env.step(Action.REST.value)

    # Helper should have spent 1 qi on STRIKE_QI against the boss
    assert helper.inventory.qi <= qi_before - 1, (
        f"Heuristic helper should auto-spend ≥1 qi attacking boss; before={qi_before}, after={helper.inventory.qi}"
    )
    assert boss.health < boss_hp_before, "Boss should have taken damage from heuristic helper"
    assert env._ep_qi_strikes_used >= 1

### 💭 Reasoning

*I'm looking at the system specifications now—it's running WSL2 with kernel 6.6.87.2, has 16 vCPUs from a Xeon Platinum processor, but WSL is only seeing 31 GiB of RAM instead of the full 64 GB available on the host, which makes sense since WSL2 defaults to allocating half the host memory.

The real bottleneck for the training workload is the Python GIL and numpy operations, not the WSL2 environment itself—the syscall and filesystem overhead is minimal for CPU-bound work, especially since the training data and checkpoints are stored in the native ext4 filesystem inside WSL rather than crossing the slow `/mnt/c/` boundary. So WSL isn't meaningfully slowing things down compared to native Linux or Windows Python, and switching to Windows directly wouldn't provide any real speedup. The actual issue to address is that WSL2 memory cap at 32 GB, which could become a constraint depending on the workload size.

The fix is straightforward: edit the `.wslconfig` file to increase the memory limit to around 56 GB, leaving some headroom for Windows itself. However, since we're currently only using 3.2 GB out of 31 GB available, RAM isn't the immediate bottleneck—CPU cores are. The real wins would come from either increasing the WSL CPU allocation (though we're likely already using all 16 logical cores available), or tuning the training parameters like n_envs to better utilize the physical cores without causing context-switching overhead from hyperthreading. Running training in the native ext4 filesystem is already happening, which is good. There's also a mention of checking subprocess configuration, but that thought got cut off.

Actually, looking at the CPU model—Xeon Platinum 8370C—this is likely running on Azure, probably a D-series VM. If that's the case, the host itself has 8 physical cores (16 logical), and the recommendations would be to update `.wslconfig` to expose all 16 vCPUs and bump memory, keep n_envs between 8 and 14 depending on what else is running, and avoid switching to Windows since the overhead isn't worth the marginal gain. If scaling becomes critical later, upgrading to a larger Azure SKU like D32s_v5 would be the move.*

<sub>⏱️ 1443m 54s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Good catch. Here's the analysis:

## What I see

| Resource | Value |
|---|---|
| OS | **WSL2** (`6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`) |
| CPU | 16 vCPUs (Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C, 8 physical cores × 2 hyperthreads) |
| RAM (visible to WSL) | **31 GiB** (3.2 used, 28 available) |
| Swap | 8 GiB |

## Answers

**1. "Is WSL slowing us down?"**
**No, not meaningfully for this workload.** Our training is CPU+numpy bound with all I/O happening inside the ext4 filesystem at `/home/...`. WSL2's overhead vs native Linux for that pattern is ~2–5%, and vs native Windows Python it's typically *faster* on numpy-heavy code (better thread scheduler). The big WSL2 perf trap is `/mnt/c/` filesystem access — and we touch zero files there. Switching to native Windows would cost a day of conda+SB3 setup pain for negligible gain.

**2. "Should I run on Windows?"**
No. Reasons to stay on WSL:
- Same Python/numpy/SB3 stack, no env churn
- bash tooling, pytest, git workflow already wired up
- Azure ML SDK and Ray RLlib (when we migrate) are first-class on Linux, painful on Windows

**3. "My devbox has 64 GB but only 31 GB shows. Why?"**
**Yes — this is real and easy to fix.** WSL2 defaults to capping memory at **50% of host RAM**. So your host indeed has ~64 GB; WSL just isn't allowed to use it. Fix: create/edit `C:\Users\\<your-username\>\.wslconfig` (in Windows, not WSL) with:

```ini
[wsl2]
memory=56GB
processors=16
swap=16GB
localhostForwarding=true
```

Then in PowerShell: `wsl --shutdown` and reopen. WSL will report 56 GB.

## Is RAM actually the bottleneck right now?

**No.** We're using **3.2 GB of 31 GB**. RAM isn't the constraint for v18 training — **CPU cores are**. With n_envs=8 we use ~8 logical CPUs out of 16 (≈4 physical cores effectively). Doubling RAM doesn't speed up PPO training; doubling cores would.

## What would actually speed up training

| Change | Speedup | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Bump `.wslconfig` memory to 56 GB | 0% (RAM not bottleneck) but **enables larger n_envs / batches** | 2 min |
| Set Windows power profile to "Best Performance" | 5–15% (prevents CPU downclock) | 1 min |
| Push `n_envs` 8 → 14 in training.yaml | ~40–60% wallclock reduction | 1 min |
| Switch to a 32-vCPU Azure SKU (D32s_v5) | ~70–90% wallclock reduction | 30 min, $$$ |
| GPU + larger batches (LSTM on CUDA) | 2–5× | half day setup, requires GPU SKU |

## Recommendation

Right now: edit `.wslconfig` (RAM headroom + explicit core count), set Windows power to "Best Performance", and bump `n_envs` to 12–14 in v18. That should cut v18 wallclock from ~6h to ~3.5h with zero infra changes. Don't bother with native Windows. When we're ready to push beyond that, the play is a bigger Azure SKU or a cloud GPU box for LSTM forward passes — both already captured in the deferred backlog.

## What this means

**The big wins are real and emergent:**
- **30% boss kill rate from a 0% baseline.** v17 never killed the boss in 20 episodes; v18 killed it in 6/20.
- **Lifespan nearly doubled.** Agents are surviving meaningfully longer.
- **Collaboration count up ~4×.** Focal is actively coordinating instead of fleeing.
- **Boss unique attackers 4.4 → 6.7** — average of ~7 distinct agents engage the boss per episode (out of 10). Collective action is emerging.
- **Training time doubled** — focal spends 48 actions/ep training (vs 24 in v17). The concave damage curve + stronger reward landscape made cultivation pay off.

**Caveats / open questions:**
1. **Focal qi-strike telemetry is all zeros**, but `attack_qi`/`attack_burst` actions ARE being chosen by focal (0.30 attacks per ep). This means focal's qi-strikes are all whiffing (no adjacent target → qi not consumed), OR the telemetry counter only tracks focal-agent strikes and the boss damage is coming from heuristic agents (which auto-spend qi). Heuristic-side attacks are not surfaced in focal-only counters — **this is a real telemetry gap to fix**.
2. **Stash usage still ~zero.** Settlement metrics didn't move. Stash + qi strategic interaction hasn't emerged yet — agents aren't learning the "deposit qi for reward vs hoard for burst attack" tradeoff. v18 was about combat tiers; settlement learning is a separate ticket.
3. **6.75 agents killed by boss per ep** — boss is still very lethal. We win 30% of the time but lose ~7 agents on average. Could lower boss damage slightly or add more tier diversity in next iteration.

## Bottom line

**v18 is a clear, large step forward on the combat axis.** First non-zero boss kill rate, doubled lifespan, 4× collaboration. Tiered qi strikes appear to have shifted policy from "flee survival" to "engage and train". Stash/settlement behavior still flat — that's the next ticket.

<sub>⏱️ 1927m 41s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

# Design: Bootstrapping territory + ally emergence

## What we already have (good news)

- **Food regenerates** (50–250 ticks). The world has the necessary dynamic, but agents can't currently *perceive* regeneration — they only see current food density in FOV, not history.
- **Groups + same-sect penalty** (`REWARD_SAME_SECT_ATTACK_PENALTY = -0.10`) already exist
- **Food sharing logic** exists (`_share_food_with_allies`) but only fires for *pre-assigned* group-mates
- **Flanking bonus** for attacking with an ally adjacent
- **`_ep_friendly_steals`** instrumentation already distinguishes friendly vs hostile stash interactions

So the substrate is there. What's missing is **emergent allegiance** — currently friends are hardcoded by `group_id`. The user is right to question that.

## The core problem

In nature, friend/foe distinction emerges from **predictable repeated interaction**, not innate labels. To get this in RL we need:
1. **Memory of who-did-what** (currently absent — agents have no per-other-agent history)
2. **A perceptual signal** that distinguishes "agent who has been peaceful near me" from "stranger"
3. **A reward shape** that pays off non-aggression with familiar agents

Without (1)+(2), the policy can't learn (3). It's the classic credit-assignment problem.

## Question-by-question

### "Do agents figure out food regeneration?"

**Today: no.** They see *current* food in FOV, not "this tile produced food 50 ticks ago". They can't distinguish a permanently-barren tile from a productive-but-depleted one. So they can't learn "camp here, food returns".

**Fix (cheap):** Add a single observation channel: **`tiles_recently_productive`** — for each tile in FOV, the count of food-units consumed there in the last K ticks (say 200). Normalized to [0,1]. This is ~5 lines of code in `_build_obs` plus a per-tile counter in `world.consume_food`. With this, the policy can learn "richness ≠ current state, richness = recent yield".

### "How can we teach agents to camp / mark territory?"

Two coupled changes:

1. **Tile familiarity channel** (per-agent): for each FOV tile, ticks-since-this-agent-last-stepped-here, exponentially decayed. Agent can perceive its own footprint.
2. **Comfort reward**: tiny (+0.001/step) bonus for standing on a tile this agent has visited in the last N steps. Trivial to add. Encourages localism without forcing immobility.

Combined with (productive-tile observation), you get emergent camping at productive patches. **No hardcoded territory marker needed** — territory IS "tiles I keep returning to that yield food".

### "How do we go from territory to allies?"

This is the hard one. My recommendation: **two-stage emergence via a "familiarity" matrix**.

#### Stage 1: passive familiarity
Every step, for each pair of agents within Chebyshev distance ≤ 3, increment a `familiarity[i,j]` counter (capped at e.g. 100, decays slowly). This is per-pair, persists across the episode. **Crucially:** if `i` attacks `j`, halve the counter and add to `hostility[i,j]`.

#### Stage 2: allegiance signal in observation
For each adjacent agent in FOV, expose two scalars: `familiarity_norm`, `hostility_norm`. The policy now has the substrate to learn "this is a familiar non-aggressor — flank with them" vs "this is a hostile — attack/flee".

#### Stage 3: reward shape that rewards reciprocity
- **Familiar-flank bonus**: existing flanking bonus, but scaled by familiarity. Flanking with a stranger: small. Flanking with a familiar: bigger.
- **Hostile-cooperation penalty**: standing still next to a high-hostility agent costs a tiny per-step penalty (you're letting your guard down with an enemy).
- **Food-share-back bonus**: if A shares food with B, and within K ticks B shares back, both get a bonus. Reciprocity = the friendship signal.

After this, **drop hardcoded `group_id` from the reward path entirely**. Sects emerge as connected components in the familiarity graph. Then the LLM (Phase 5) can read the matrix and *name* the emergent cliques as sects.

### Animal/anthropology grounding

Your monkey-ancestor intuition is right: the basis is **predictability + reciprocity**. Monkey troops don't have ID badges; they have stable bilateral histories. The "in-group" is just the connected subgraph of repeated peaceful interaction. Our familiarity matrix is exactly this, in machine-readable form.

The trickiest invariant from real animals is **forgiveness without exploitation**. Hostility must decay (otherwise one mistake is permanent), but slowly enough that defectors aren't immediately re-trusted. Suggest exp decay with half-life ~500 ticks.

### "How rigid should territory be?"

Don't bake in rigidity. Just give agents perception + reward gradient and let them choose. Some policies will discover camping; others (with low strength) will discover nomadism. Both should be viable so the system explores the policy space.

## Suggested ticket sequence (cheap → ambitious)

These are independent — each is ship-able alone and gives a measurable signal.

| # | Ticket | What | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | `tile-recency-obs` | Add productive-tile-recency channel to `_build_obs` | 1 day |
| **2** | `tile-familiarity-obs` | Add per-agent tile-visit-recency channel | 1 day |
| **3** | `comfort-reward` | Tiny bonus for standing on familiar tiles | half day |
| **4** | `pairwise-familiarity-matrix` | Add `familiarity[i,j]` + `hostility[i,j]` state, expose to obs for FOV agents | 2 days |
| **5** | `reciprocity-reward` | Familiar-flank, food-share-back, hostile-stand-still penalty | 1 day |
| **6** | `drop-hardcoded-groups` | Remove `group_id` from reward path; rely on emergent familiarity | 1 day + tests |
| **7** | `territory-eval-metrics` | New telemetry: home-range area, time-on-home-tiles, dominant-clique-size | half day |

**Recommendation: do 1 + 2 + 3 first** as a single PR. That gives the territory substrate without changing ally semantics. Run a training+eval cycle to see if camping emerges. *Then* tackle the familiarity matrix (4–6) — that's the bigger change and you want a working baseline first.

## Open question for you

Two design choices I'd flag before implementing:

**A. Familiarity matrix size.** With 10 agents per env it's a 10×10 matrix — trivial. But if we ever scale to 50+ agents per env, the obs space (each agent sees N familiarity scalars) explodes. Are we committing to ≤20 agents per env for the medium term? If so, the matrix approach is fine. If not, we need a different mechanism (e.g., per-agent embedding learned by an attention head — bigger lift).

**B. Hostility persistence across episodes?** Real-world allegiances persist for years. RL episodes are 2000 steps. Do we want familiarity/hostility to persist across episodes (per-seed simulation continuity), or reset every episode (faster credit assignment, less realistic)? My instinct: reset for now, revisit when we add the LLM layer in Phase 5 — at that point the LLM can serve as cross-episode memory.

Want me to scope out tickets 1–3 (territory substrate) as the immediate next step, or zoom in on a specific decision first?

### 💭 Reasoning

*I see that `_help_received` currently stores just a single timestamp for each recipient-helper pair, tracking only the most recent help event for the reciprocity bonus calculation. To properly support the full history of exchanges between pairs, I need to restructure this into a complete per-pair history rather than a single pointer. <sub>⏱️ 1950m 54s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Crisp answers in the same order:

## 1. Remove sect identity & enforcement entirely — yes, agreed

Scope I'd actually rip out:
- `Agent.sect_id` field
- `SectConfig` + `SectRegistry` (`murimsim/sect.py`) — kept as YAML config only if the LLM later needs *names*
- `REWARD_SAME_SECT_ATTACK_PENALTY` and both call sites in `multi_env.py:1526–1541`
- `_sect_config` plumbing in `CombatEnv.__init__` and `reset`
- `ep_sect_id` in info dict
- Existing sect tests deleted (or rewritten as "no sects" sanity tests)

What stays: `_groups` (which is just contiguous-index buckets — purely a spawn-time clustering primitive, no identity), the food-share logic (rewrites to use familiarity), the flanking bonus mechanic itself.

This is a clean ~half-day surgery. Tests will go red where they assert sect penalties — those tests should be deleted, not updated, since the behavior is being removed.

## 2. Flanking bonus — make it learned, but with a runway

**My honest opinion: pure PPO will *not* discover flanking on its own in our timescales.** Reasons:
- Flanking requires two agents to coordinate spatial positioning across multiple turns to set up a single high-reward attack. The credit assignment chain is ~3–5 steps long with sparse reward.
- Both agents need to simultaneously deviate from a locally-optimal action (single attack) toward a globally-better one (positioning). That's a coordination equilibrium PPO finds very hard without shaping.
- No real-world agent learns flanking from scratch either — it's almost always taught.

So my recommendation: **keep the flanking bonus, but make its magnitude scale with familiarity** (per stage 3 of the earlier design). That way the *tactic* is still externally rewarded, but *who you flank with* becomes a learned choice. We get the best of both: the policy doesn't have to discover flanking from scratch (would never converge), but it *does* have to learn whom to trust as a flanking partner.

When we move to MAPPO/CTDE with centralized critic in Phase 4+, *then* it becomes plausible to drop the flanking bonus entirely and let the centralized value function discover it. Not before.

## 3. Per-other-agent memory — partially done, expand it

We **already have** `_help_received[recipient][helper] = step_when_helped` at line 283. But it's only a single timestamp per pair (most recent help), and only tracks helps, not attacks/steals. So we built the skeleton, never fleshed it out.

Concrete proposal — your "score the last 5–10 actions" instinct is right and the cheapest implementation:

```python
# Per-agent ring buffer of recent interactions with every other agent.
# _interactions[i][j] = deque of (step, kind, magnitude), maxlen=10
# kinds: SHARE (+1.0), HELP_FLANK (+0.5), ATTACK (-1.0), STEAL (-0.7), KILL (-2.0)
# affinity[i][j] = decayed sum (newer events weighted higher)
```

This is your LRU idea (point 4) baked in: `maxlen=10` deque is exactly an LRU. Old events drop off automatically.

**On manifestation (your hard question):** I'd avoid `social_dependency` as a trait — it adds a parameter without a clear policy-side learning signal. Instead, expose `affinity[i][j]` for adjacent agents in the observation (one scalar per FOV agent, normalized to [-1, 1]). Then let three reward shapes do the work:

- **Familiar-flank scaling**: existing flanking bonus × `max(0, affinity[i,j])`. Flanking with a stranger: 1× current. Flanking with a high-affinity ally: 2× current.
- **Reciprocal-share bonus**: A shares food with B, B reciprocates within 50 ticks → both get +0.05. Builds friendship via reciprocity, not declaration.
- **Background betrayal cost**: attacking an agent with affinity \> 0.5 costs an extra −0.20 (you broke trust). This replaces the sect penalty.

No `social_dependency` parameter. No "invite friendship" action. The policy just learns "high-affinity neighbor = good flanking partner = better reward". Friendship emerges as a *behavioral* pattern (these two move together, share, flank together), not a declared status.

## 4. LRU eviction — exactly right

`collections.deque(maxlen=10)` per pair gives you free LRU. Old interactions silently fall off. No explicit decay code needed; the windowing IS the decay. If we want graceful (not cliff) decay, we just exponentially weight by age inside the deque when computing the affinity scalar — 5 lines of code.

## 5. Reset per seed — confirmed, simplest path

Both `_interactions` and the derived affinity matrix reset on `env.reset()`. We can revisit cross-episode persistence in Phase 5 when LLM reasoning enters the loop.

## What I propose as the next ticket bundle

One coherent PR. Order matters because each step depends on prior:

| # | Step | Files | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Rip out sect identity (Agent.sect_id, sect penalty, sect_config plumbing, ep_sect_id) | agent.py, multi_env.py, tests | half day |
| **B** | Add `_interactions[i][j]: deque(maxlen=10)` + `affinity_score(i,j)` helper | multi_env.py | 1 day |
| **C** | Hook interaction recording into 4 events: food-share, attack, steal, flank-assist | multi_env.py (5 call sites) | half day |
| **D** | Expose `affinity_to_neighbor` in `_build_obs` (1 scalar per adjacent agent slot) | multi_env.py | half day |
| **E** | Update reward shapes: scale flank bonus by affinity, reciprocal-share bonus, betrayal penalty | multi_env.py | half day |
| **F** | Telemetry: `ep_max_affinity_pair`, `ep_avg_pos_affinity`, `ep_betrayals` | multi_env.py | half day |
| **G** | Delete sect tests; add affinity tests (matrix grows on share, decays via maxlen, attack flips sign) | tests/ | 1 day |
| **H** | Train v19 from scratch (action space unchanged → could even warm-start from v18) | config + run | 3h wallclock |

**Total: ~4 days dev + 3h training.** Single coherent change, all the conceptual pieces interlock.

## Open question for you before I start

**One thing I want to flag**: dropping sect identity means the v18 checkpoint can still load (action space = 17, unchanged), but v18 was trained in a world where `sect_id == "none"` for all agents anyway (no sect_config was passed to training envs). So we should be able to **warm-start v19 from v18** — much faster convergence. Confirm OK, or do you want v19 from scratch?

Want me to start with step A (the sect rip-out) as a standalone PR so we can land it fast and verify nothing breaks, then queue B–H as the second PR? Or one big bundle?

131.     env = CombatEnv(config=config, n_agents=args.agents, seed=args.seed)
132.     env_obs_size: int = env.observation_space.shape[0]
133. 
134.     # Assign round-robin sect IDs for viewer coloring (no home-region spawning in recording mode)
135.     def _assign_sect_ids() -> None:
136.         for i, agent in enumerate(env._agents):
137.             agent.sect_id = DEFAULT_SECTS.by_index(i).sect_id
138. 
139.     # Compat shim: if model was trained on a smaller obs space (e.g. M3=209 vs M4=234),
140.     # strip the extra features by dropping the enemy-stash channel from the stash section.
141.     # Layout: resources(100) + agents(75) + stash(N) + stats(9)
142.     # M3 stash was 1 channel (25 values); M4 stash is 2 channels (50 values, interleaved).
143.     def _compat_obs(obs: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
144.         if model_obs_size is None or model_obs_size == env_obs_size:
145.             return obs
146.         # Determine stash sizes
147.         static_prefix = 100 + 75   # resource + agent grids
148.         stats_size = 9
149.         env_stash_size = env_obs_size - static_prefix - stats_size
150.         model_stash_size = model_obs_size - static_prefix - stats_size
151.         if env_stash_size > model_stash_size and env_stash_size % model_stash_size == 0:
152.             # Interleaved channels: take channel-0 (my_stash) values
153.             n_stash_cells = model_stash_size
154.             n_channels = env_stash_size // model_stash_size
155.             stash_flat = obs[static_prefix : static_prefix + env_stash_size]
156.             stash_ch0 = stash_flat.reshape(n_stash_cells, n_channels)[:, 0]
157.             return np.concatenate([obs[:static_prefix], stash_ch0, obs[-stats_size:]])
158.         # Fallback: truncate
159.         return obs[:model_obs_size]
160. 
161.     obs, _ = env.reset(seed=args.seed)
162.     _assign_sect_ids()
163. 
164.     # Enable full combat immediately (skip curriculum ramp for interesting replays)
165.     if not args.no_combat:
166.         env._global_step_count = env._curriculum_ramp_steps
167. 
168.     # Default filename: combat_<model_stem>.jsonl (e.g. combat_v16.jsonl from limbic_lstm_v16_final.zip)

791.         agent: Agent,

793.         inv_food_prev: int = 0,
794.     ) -> float:
795.         """Compute shaped per-step reward.
796. 
797.         Stage 5 additions:
798.         - Potential-based inventory security: reward Δ(food_in_hand) so gathering
799.           is worth more than the raw food-gathered bonus alone.
800.         - Starvation proximity penalty: discourages drifting into the danger zone
801.           rather than waiting until death.
802.         - Exploration is survival-gated (passed in pre-scaled by caller).
803. 
804.         Stage 6b additions:
805.         - Health recovery bonus: rewards regaining health after eating or resting.
806.         """
807.         reward = REWARD_ALIVE
808.         hunger_relief = hunger_prev - agent.hunger
809.         if hunger_relief > 0:
810.             reward += REWARD_HUNGER_RELIEF_SCALE * hunger_relief
811.         reward += REWARD_FOOD_GATHERED_SCALE * food_gathered
812.         reward += REWARD_HAZARD_DAMAGE_SCALE * hazard_damage
813.         reward += exploration_reward
814.         # Potential-based inventory shaping: φ(s) = food_in_hand / INV_SECURITY_CAP
815.         inv_delta = (agent.inventory.food - inv_food_prev) / INV_SECURITY_CAP
816.         reward += REWARD_INV_SECURITY_SCALE * inv_delta
817.         # Starvation proximity penalty
818.         if agent.hunger > STARVATION_THRESHOLD:
819.             reward += PENALTY_STARVATION_APPROACH * (agent.hunger - STARVATION_THRESHOLD)
820.         # Low-health danger penalty: continuous signal every step health is critically low.
821.         # Scales with distance below gate — the closer to death, the louder the signal.

### 💭 Reasoning

*I'm laying out the implementation strategy now. For tracking interactions between agents, I'll use a nested dictionary structure where each pair stores a bounded deque of recent interactions—keeping the last 10 events with their step, type, and magnitude. Then I'll compute an affinity score based on these historical interactions to inform how agents influence each other.

The affinity calculation applies a time-decay weight that diminishes older events linearly toward zero over a defined horizon, then normalizes the weighted sum to a [-1, 1] range. I'm mapping four key interaction types—food sharing, attacks, stealing, and flanking—each with their own magnitude values that reflect their social impact. I need to hook into the existing code at specific points where these events occur: the food-sharing function, the attack resolution step, the steal mechanics, and the flanking bonus logic. For consistency, I'll record interactions bidirectionally so both participants have a record of what happened between them. Now I'm exposing affinity values in the observation by adding a new channel to the agent window — that bumps the observation space from 264 to 289 dimensions, which unfortunately breaks warm-starting from v18. For the channel itself, I'm normalizing affinity from [-1, 1] to [0, 1] by applying the formula (affinity + 1.0) / 2.0.

Then I'm updating the reward shaping to incorporate affinity in three ways: scaling the flanking bonus by the average affinity toward flanking partners, adding a reciprocal share bonus when both agents share with each other within a time window, and penalizing betrayal when the focal agent attacks someone with high affinity.

For telemetry, I need to track episode-level metrics like the strongest affinity pair, average positive affinity, betrayal count, and friendly shares — so I'm adding episode counters that reset each run. My implementation plan is to add the affinity constants and deque configuration at the top, update the observation dimensions, initialize an interaction tracking structure in the base environment class, and then build out helper methods to record and query interactions.

Now I'm checking how the existing food sharing and stealing mechanics pass agent indices so I can hook the affinity system into those same events.*

### 💭 Reasoning

*Now I'm settling on the implementation structure — I need to put the interaction tracking on `MultiAgentEnv` since that's where food sharing happens, and since the observation builder is also there, I can keep all the changes localized to that parent class.

For the constants, I'm defining a 10-event LRU window per agent pair, a 200-step decay horizon so older interactions fade out, and normalizing affinity to roughly [-1, 1] by dividing by 5. The interaction magnitudes are +1.0 for sharing, +0.5 for flanking assists, -1.0 for attacks, and -0.7 for steals. I'm also keeping the existing reciprocity mechanism in `_help_received` separate since it's orthogonal and already working.

Defining the interaction recording method...

For affinity computation, I walk through the deque for each pair, apply linear age decay, sum weighted values, divide by the norm constant, and clamp to [-1, 1]. The observation channel maps this to [0, 1] by taking the mean affinity when multiple agents occupy the same tile.

On rewards, coordinated attacks get a multiplier based on flanker affinity—strangers stay at 1.0× while strong allies reach up to 2.0×. I'm adding a small +0.03 bonus when both sharer and recipient have positive affinity, keeping the existing share threshold logic untouched. For betrayals, when an agent attacks someone with affinity above 0.3, I subtract 0.20 from the reward (gated on actual damage dealt), using a lower threshold to make the penalty more sensitive. Finally, I'm tracking `ep_betrayals` in the terminal info for telemetry.

1205.         0=present, 1=health (normalised), 2=strength, 3=sociability.
1206.         Monsters get sociability=0 and strength as raw value (typically ~1.6

1213.         ax, ay = agent.position

### 💬 Copilot

## Blocking Issues

1. **This does not create emergent allegiance; it creates a transient reward tag.**  
   **Impact:** Since non-focal agents do not learn and apparently do not condition their behavior on affinity, “allegiance” has no strategic consequences except focal reward shaping. The policy can learn local heuristics like “don’t attack recent sharers” or “flank near positive-affinity bodies,” but not coalition formation.  
   **Fix:** Make heuristic agents consume affinity too: share/assist/retaliate/avoid based on it. Better: train more than focal-only, at least via rotating focal/IPPO/self-play.

2. **Credit assignment for mutual-share bonus is weak/noisy.**  
   **Impact:** If focal receives food because a scripted agent decided to share, rewarding focal teaches the focal to be hungry/near scripted sharers, not to build allegiance. If focal is sharer, it already gets share reward, so the added bonus may just double-count.  
   **Fix:** Only give mutual-share bonus when focal is the actor whose previous actions plausibly caused the affinity, or split into actor-specific rewards: reward focal-as-sharer; maybe survival benefit only for focal-as-recipient.

3. **Observation loses identity, so pairwise memory may be unlearnable.**  
   **Impact:** Affinity is pair-specific, but the obs gives only tile-level averaged affinity. If multiple agents overlap/cluster, identity is aliased. The policy cannot reliably know “this is the same ally as before,” especially without stable IDs or embeddings.  
   **Fix:** Add stable per-agent local IDs/relative slots, or expose top-k nearby agents with features including affinity. Mean-over-tile is too lossy for allegiance.

4. **Symmetric recording is probably wrong for emergence.**  
   **Impact:** It conflates “I helped you,” “you helped me,” “I hurt you,” and “you hurt me.” Receiving a share increases the recipient’s and sharer’s affinity identically, even though only one paid a cost. Attacking someone reduces both sides identically, even though attacker and victim should update differently. This destroys important social asymmetries: debt, grievance, exploitation, trust.  
   **Fix:** Use directional memory. Example: `affinity[i][j]` means i’s attitude toward j. Share: recipient→sharer positive, maybe sharer→recipient small positive. Attack: victim→attacker strongly negative, attacker→victim maybe small negative or unchanged.

## Non-Blocking Issues

5. **200-step decay makes “allegiance” too short-lived for 2000-step episodes.**  
   **Impact:** This is more like recent mood than allegiance. Any coalition evaporates after 10% of episode length unless constantly refreshed. That encourages affinity farming loops, not durable bonds.  
   **Fix:** Use two traces: short-term interaction trace and long-term relationship trace. E.g. fast decay for combat coordination, slow decay over 1000–2000 steps for allegiance.

6. **`maxlen=10` plus decay is mostly okay mechanically, but semantically odd.**  
   **Impact:** Stale events can sit in the deque doing nothing; not harmful unless telemetry counts raw events. But high-frequency interactions can evict meaningful older events before decay would. A burst of shares/attacks can saturate or erase relationship history too quickly.  
   **Fix:** Prefer exponentially decayed scalar accumulators per directed pair instead of deques. Simpler, cheaper, clearer credit dynamics.

7. **Betrayal threshold 0.3 is likely too easy under symmetric share.**  
   **Impact:** Two fresh shares produce ~0.4 affinity. With scripted agents sharing, focal can accidentally cross the betrayal threshold without intentionally forming a bond. Then ordinary combat choices get penalized.  
   **Fix:** Raise threshold or require repeated positive interactions across time, e.g. positive affinity sustained for N steps or at least 3–5 positive events. Directional memory would also help.

8. **Betrayal penalty may produce attack avoidance, not loyalty.**  
   **Impact:** If positive-affinity agents are common food sharers/flankers, focal may learn “avoid attacking agents near me” rather than “protect allies.” Since there is no reward for defending allies, only a penalty for attacking them, allegiance becomes inhibition.  
   **Fix:** Add positive agency: reward defending high-affinity agents, assisting their fights, sharing when they are hungry, or retaliating against their attackers.

9. **Friendly-flank bonus can be gamed by proximity, not coordination.**  
   **Impact:** If flanker presence is enough, focal gets extra reward for attacking while a positive-affinity agent happens to stand nearby. That may teach “attack near friends,” not actual coordinated combat.  
   **Fix:** Require the flanker to have recently attacked/defended against the same target, or require target engagement from both agents within a small window.

10. **Reward asymmetry may be too punitive relative to combat rewards.**  
   **Impact:** `-0.20` betrayal versus max extra `+0.10` friendly flank may suppress combat with any positive-affinity agent, especially if accidental affinity is common. If attack rewards/damage rewards are small, this can collapse aggression. If attack payoff is larger, betrayal becomes just a one-time tax.  
   **Fix:** Calibrate against actual attack reward/damage value. Better: scale betrayal penalty by relationship strength and damage dealt, not a flat cliff at 0.3.

## Suggestions

11. **Make affinity affect environment dynamics, not only reward/obs.**  
   If affinity changes share probability, assist probability, retaliation, avoidance, stash access, or target selection, then the focal has a reason to manage relationships beyond shaped reward.

12. **Telemetry is missing policy-relevant failure modes.**  
   Add:
   - attacks on neutral/negative targets  
   - positive-affinity duration per pair  
   - affinity caused by focal action vs heuristic action  
   - share received vs share given  
   - betrayal penalty total  
   - friendly-flank reward total  
   These reveal whether the policy is farming scripted generosity.

13. **Training from scratch for v19 is acceptable, but only if this design is worth the reset.**  
   The obs break is fine technically. The risk is spending a full fresh run on a signal that cannot produce real allegiance because other agents are fixed and non-responsive.

14. **Current design likely learns “relationship-shaped survival heuristics,” not emergent sects.**  
   That may still be useful as Plan B, but do not overinterpret results. If you want emergence, affinity needs bidirectionality, persistence, identity, and behavioral consequences.

<sub>⏱️ 1986m 51s</sub>

### 💭 Reasoning

*The critique makes solid points, so I'm separating what I can fix now from what needs deferral. The directional memory issue is actionable—I need to implement asymmetric affinity updates where sharing and attacking have different effects depending on direction, like making the recipient's view of the sharer improve more than vice versa.

For decay, I'm pushing the horizon from 200 to 1000 steps to keep relationships stable longer. The betrayal threshold moves from 0.3 to 0.5 to require more sustained positive history. On the observation side, I'll use max magnitude across tiles instead of averaging to preserve strong signals, though full top-k indexing is a bigger refactor I'm deferring.

For the accumulator, I'm torn between the simpler exponential decay approach versus the LRU deque the user originally requested—the decay accomplishes the forgetting mechanic they wanted, but I need to reconcile that with their explicit preference...

Actually, I think exponential decay gets the job done more efficiently. I'll note the tradeoff in my response and see if they're open to it. The rest of the fixes are straightforward: asymmetric event magnitudes for relationships, deferring the heuristic integration and mutual-share refinements to later, and accepting the tile aliasing as a documented limitation for now.*

| Mutual-share double-counts | **Adopt** — only reward focal-as-sharer |
| Betrayal threshold 0.3 too low | **Adopt** — bump to 0.5 |
| Tile-avg loses identity | **Partial** — use tile-MAX (preserves strongest signal); defer top-k refactor |

664.     def _group_cohesion_reward(self, agent_idx: int) -> float:
665.         """Return a per-tick reward for each live group member within GROUP_COHESION_RANGE.
666. 
667.         Uses Chebyshev distance (consistent with 8-direction combat range).
668.         Incentivises staying physically close to group members rather than
669.         drifting apart after forming a group.
670.         """
671.         group = self._get_group(agent_idx)
672.         if group is None:
673.             return 0.0
674.         ax, ay = self._agents[agent_idx].position
675.         nearby_count = 0
676.         for ally_idx in group:
677.             if ally_idx == agent_idx:
678.                 continue
679.             ally = self._agents[ally_idx]
680.             if not ally.alive:
681.                 continue
682.             ox, oy = ally.position
683.             if max(abs(ox - ax), abs(oy - ay)) <= GROUP_COHESION_RANGE:
684.                 nearby_count += 1
685.         return REWARD_GROUP_COHESION_PER_ALLY * nearby_count

687.     def _try_food_share(self, sharer_idx: int, recipient_idx: int) -> bool:
688.         """Attempt to share one food unit from sharer to recipient.
689. 
690.         Succeeds only if:
691.           - Recipient is alive, in the same group as sharer, and critically hungry.
692.           - Sharer has food in inventory.
693.           - Reciprocity roll passes (boosted if recipient helped sharer recently).
694. 
695.         Returns True if food was actually transferred.
696.         """
697.         sharer = self._agents[sharer_idx]
698.         recipient = self._agents[recipient_idx]
699. 
700.         if not (sharer.alive and recipient.alive):
701.             return False
702.         if self._get_group(sharer_idx) != self._get_group(recipient_idx):
703.             return False
704.         if self._get_group(sharer_idx) is None:
705.             return False
706.         if recipient.hunger < SHARE_HUNGER_THRESHOLD:
707.             return False
708.         if sharer.inventory.food == 0:
709.             return False
710. 
711.         # Reciprocity: did the recipient help the sharer recently?
712.         last_help = self._help_received.get(sharer_idx, {}).get(recipient_idx, -RECIPROCITY_WINDOW - 1)
713.         boosted = (self._ep_step_count - last_help) <= RECIPROCITY_WINDOW
714.         threshold = RECIPROCITY_BOOSTED if boosted else RECIPROCITY_BASE
715. 
716.         if self._rng.random() > threshold:
717.             return False
718. 
719.         # Transfer one food unit
720.         sharer.inventory.food -= 1

# ─── v19: Emergent allegiance / affinity matrix tests ────────────────────────


def test_affinity_starts_at_zero() -> None:
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    assert env._affinity(0, 1) == 0.0
    assert env._affinity(1, 0) == 0.0
    assert env._affinity(0, 0) == 0.0  # self-affinity always 0


def test_affinity_is_directional_attack() -> None:
    """Victim builds stronger hostility toward attacker than attacker → victim."""
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    attacker, victim = env._agents[0], env._agents[1]
    attacker.position = (5, 5)
    victim.position = (5, 6)
    victim.health = 1.0
    env._do_attack(attacker)
    aff_victim_to_attacker = env._affinity(1, 0)
    aff_attacker_to_victim = env._affinity(0, 1)
    assert aff_victim_to_attacker < aff_attacker_to_victim < 0.0
    # Victim's hostility magnitude should be larger than attacker's.
    assert abs(aff_victim_to_attacker) > abs(aff_attacker_to_victim)


def test_affinity_decays_over_time() -> None:
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    env._record_affinity_event(0, 1, actor_to_other=1.0, other_to_actor=1.0)
    aff_now = env._affinity(0, 1)
    assert aff_now > 0.0
    env._ep_step_count += 1000  # advance time
    aff_later = env._affinity(0, 1)
    assert aff_later < aff_now * 0.6  # decayed substantially


def test_affinity_self_pair_ignored() -> None:
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    env._record_affinity_event(0, 0, actor_to_other=10.0, other_to_actor=10.0)
    assert env._affinity(0, 0) == 0.0


def test_affinity_clears_on_reset() -> None:
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    env._record_affinity_event(0, 1, actor_to_other=1.0, other_to_actor=1.0)
    assert env._affinity(0, 1) > 0.0
    env.reset(seed=1)
    assert env._affinity(0, 1) == 0.0


def test_affinity_in_obs_channel() -> None:
    """Obs channel 4 (affinity) should reflect focal→neighbour relationship."""
    from murimsim.rl.multi_env import OBS_RESOURCE_GRID_SIZE, OBS_AGENT_GRID_SIZE
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal_idx = env._focal_idx
    other_idx = (focal_idx + 1) % env._n_agents
    focal = env._agents[focal_idx]
    other = env._agents[other_idx]
    fx, fy = focal.position
    other.position = (min(fx + 1, env._world.grid_size - 1), fy)
    # Big positive affinity event toward `other`
    env._record_affinity_event(focal_idx, other_idx, actor_to_other=5.0, other_to_actor=5.0)
    obs = env._build_obs(focal_idx)
    agent_grid = obs[OBS_RESOURCE_GRID_SIZE:OBS_RESOURCE_GRID_SIZE + OBS_AGENT_GRID_SIZE].reshape(5, 5, 5)
    # Affinity channel mapped from [-1,1] to [0,1]; +5/AFFINITY_NORM(=5) clipped to 1 → 1.0
    affinity_max = agent_grid[:, :, 4].max()
    assert affinity_max > 0.9, f"Expected affinity channel max ≈1.0, got {affinity_max}"


def test_terminal_info_emits_v19_keys() -> None:
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    info = {}
    for _ in range(2050):
        _, _, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(int(Action.STAY.value))
        if terminated or truncated:
            break
    # Either terminal or hit max steps — terminal info should be populated when ep ends
    if "ep_betrayal_count" in info:
        assert info["ep_betrayal_count"] == 0
        assert info["ep_friendly_flank_count"] == 0
        assert "ep_focal_max_affinity" in info
        assert "ep_focal_min_affinity" in info

# ─── v19: Affinity event-recording integration tests ─────────────────────────


def _force_group(env, *idxs):
    """Force the given agent indices into the same group (skip RNG/COLLABORATE)."""
    group = list(idxs)
    env._groups.append(group)
    for i in idxs:
        env._agent_to_group[i] = len(env._groups) - 1


def test_affinity_recorded_on_food_share() -> None:
    """_try_food_share must update directional affinity (recipient learns more)."""
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    sharer_idx, recipient_idx = 0, 1
    sharer = env._agents[sharer_idx]
    recipient = env._agents[recipient_idx]
    sharer.inventory.food = 5
    recipient.hunger = 1.0  # critical
    _force_group(env, sharer_idx, recipient_idx)
    # Force reciprocity roll to succeed by stacking RNG calls; loop until success.
    for _ in range(50):
        env._ep_step_count += 1
        if env._try_food_share(sharer_idx, recipient_idx):
            break
    assert env._affinity(recipient_idx, sharer_idx) > 0.0
    assert env._affinity(sharer_idx, recipient_idx) > 0.0
    # Recipient should feel stronger gratitude than sharer's investment.
    assert env._affinity(recipient_idx, sharer_idx) > env._affinity(sharer_idx, recipient_idx)


def test_affinity_recorded_on_steal() -> None:
    """STEAL handler must update affinity (victim resents thief strongly)."""
    from murimsim.actions import Action
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal_idx = env._focal_idx
    victim_idx = (focal_idx + 1) % env._n_agents
    focal = env._agents[focal_idx]
    victim = env._agents[victim_idx]
    # Place focal on victim's stash tile with food in stash.
    victim.inventory.food = 0
    env._stash_registry.deposit(victim, 3)
    stashes = env._stash_registry.get_stashes_for_owner(victim.agent_id)
    assert stashes
    focal.position = stashes[0].position
    env.step(int(Action.STEAL.value))
    assert env._affinity(victim_idx, focal_idx) < 0.0
    assert env._affinity(focal_idx, victim_idx) < 0.0
    assert abs(env._affinity(victim_idx, focal_idx)) > abs(env._affinity(focal_idx, victim_idx))


def test_affinity_flank_bond_recorded() -> None:
    """When attacker hits target with a flanking ally, attacker↔ally affinity goes up."""
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    attacker, ally, target = env._agents[0], env._agents[1], env._agents[2]
    attacker.position = (5, 5)
    ally.position = (5, 4)        # adjacent to target
    target.position = (5, 6)      # adjacent to attacker AND ally (Chebyshev)
    target.health = 1.0
    _force_group(env, 0, 1)       # group required for adjacency to count as flank
    env._do_attack(attacker)
    aff_atk_to_ally = env._affinity(0, 1)
    aff_ally_to_atk = env._affinity(1, 0)
    assert aff_atk_to_ally > 0.0, "attacker should bond with flanking ally"
    assert aff_ally_to_atk > 0.0, "flanking ally should bond with attacker"


def test_attack_zero_damage_does_not_record_affinity() -> None:
    """No adjacent target → no affinity change (guards against phantom updates)."""
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    a, b = env._agents[0], env._agents[1]
    a.position = (1, 1)
    b.position = (15, 15)         # far away
    env._do_attack(a)
    assert env._affinity(0, 1) == 0.0
    assert env._affinity(1, 0) == 0.0


def test_betrayal_penalty_and_telemetry() -> None:
    """Focal attacking a high-affinity target → betrayal penalty + counter incremented."""
    from murimsim.rl.multi_env import (
        AFFINITY_BETRAY_THRESHOLD, AFFINITY_NORM, PENALTY_BETRAYAL,
    )
    from murimsim.actions import Action
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal_idx = env._focal_idx
    target_idx = (focal_idx + 1) % env._n_agents
    focal = env._agents[focal_idx]
    target = env._agents[target_idx]
    focal.position = (5, 5)
    target.position = (5, 6)
    target.health = 1.0
    # Pre-load focal→target affinity above the betrayal threshold.
    raw_value = (AFFINITY_BETRAY_THRESHOLD + 0.2) * AFFINITY_NORM
    env._record_affinity_event(focal_idx, target_idx,
                               actor_to_other=raw_value, other_to_actor=0.0)
    assert env._affinity(focal_idx, target_idx) >= AFFINITY_BETRAY_THRESHOLD
    pre_count = env._ep_betrayal_count
    _, reward, _, _, _ = env.step(int(Action.ATTACK.value))
    assert env._ep_betrayal_count == pre_count + 1
    # Reward should include the negative betrayal penalty (other terms may push it up,
    # but penalty must have been applied — check via direct value bound).
    assert reward <= 1.0 + PENALTY_BETRAYAL + 1.0  # loose bound, just sanity


def test_friendly_flank_telemetry_increments() -> None:
    """Focal flanking with a positive-affinity ally bumps ep_friendly_flank_count."""
    from murimsim.rl.multi_env import AFFINITY_NORM
    from murimsim.actions import Action
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal_idx = env._focal_idx
    ally_idx = (focal_idx + 1) % env._n_agents
    target_idx = (focal_idx + 2) % env._n_agents
    focal, ally, target = env._agents[focal_idx], env._agents[ally_idx], env._agents[target_idx]
    focal.position = (5, 5)
    ally.position = (5, 4)
    target.position = (5, 6)
    target.health = 1.0
    _force_group(env, focal_idx, ally_idx)
    # Pre-load focal→ally positive affinity.
    env._record_affinity_event(focal_idx, ally_idx,
                               actor_to_other=2.0 * AFFINITY_NORM, other_to_actor=0.0)
    pre = env._ep_friendly_flank_count
    env.step(int(Action.ATTACK.value))
    assert env._ep_friendly_flank_count == pre + 1


def test_mutual_share_bonus_only_for_focal_as_sharer() -> None:
    """Focal-as-recipient must NOT receive food_share_reward (critique #2 fix).

    Replays a step where focal is hungry recipient and another agent is sharer.
    The reward should NOT contain REWARD_FOOD_SHARE term.
    """
    from murimsim.rl.multi_env import REWARD_FOOD_SHARE
    from murimsim.actions import Action
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    focal_idx = env._focal_idx
    sharer_idx = (focal_idx + 1) % env._n_agents
    focal = env._agents[focal_idx]
    sharer = env._agents[sharer_idx]
    # Focal is the hungry recipient
    focal.hunger = 1.0
    focal.inventory.food = 0
    sharer.inventory.food = 5
    sharer.hunger = 0.0
    # Place adjacent + grouped
    focal.position = (5, 5)
    sharer.position = (5, 6)
    _force_group(env, focal_idx, sharer_idx)
    # Run several steps with focal doing nothing harmful (REST), let heuristic share.
    rewards = []
    for _ in range(10):
        focal.hunger = 1.0  # keep hungry to keep eligible
        focal.inventory.food = 0
        _, r, term, _, _ = env.step(int(Action.REST.value))
        rewards.append(r)
        if term:
            break
    # Focal-as-recipient bonus removed: no single step reward should equal/exceed
    # REWARD_FOOD_SHARE driven purely by being received-to. Loose check:
    # No single step should contain a +REWARD_FOOD_SHARE attributable to recipient role.
    # (We can't perfectly isolate other reward terms, but with REST + hungry + no
    # combat the base reward is dominated by hunger penalty. A leaked +0.05 share
    # would manifest as a step with reward noticeably higher than a baseline.)
    assert max(rewards) < REWARD_FOOD_SHARE, (
        f"Focal-as-recipient share bonus appears to leak through: max step reward "
        f"{max(rewards)} >= REWARD_FOOD_SHARE {REWARD_FOOD_SHARE}"
    )
PYEOF
echo "done"

<sub>⏱️ 1997m 25s</sub>

### 💭 Reasoning

*I see the issue now — the mutual bonus is triggering because each share operation records affinity, and when the loop iterates again with remaining food, it detects that positive affinity and fires the mutual condition on the second share. The affinity gets written after the first successful share, so the second iteration sees it and applies the bonus. I see the issue now — the affinity check happens after `_try_food_share` updates it, so in the actual code every focal share gets the mutual bonus because the affinity was just recorded. That's a real bug where the bonus logic assumes pre-existing affinity but actually triggers on freshly-recorded affinity from the same share event.*

<sub>⏱️ 2564m 31s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

# v19 Eval Report (vs v18 baseline, both 20 eps, boss enabled, seed 42)

## Headline metrics

| Metric | v18 | v19 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ep_lifespan** | 71.4 | **79.7 ± 51.8** | **+12%** |
| **ep_reproductions** | 2.60 | **3.15** | **+21%** |
| ep_boss_killed | 0.30 | 0.30 | flat |
| ep_boss_attacks_landed | 12.15 | 12.20 | flat |
| ep_boss_unique_attackers | 6.70 | 6.85 | flat |
| ep_focal_collaborate_count | 0.95 | **0.75** | **−21%** |
| action_train | 37.0 | 40.1 | +8% |

## v19 affinity telemetry (the whole point of this run)

| Metric | Value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| ep_betrayal_count | **0.000** | Focal never attacked a high-affinity target |
| ep_friendly_flank_count | **0.000** | Focal never flanked with positive-affinity ally |
| ep_focal_max_affinity | **0.037** | Strongest relationship ≈ zero |
| ep_focal_min_affinity | **−0.005** | Most negative relationship ≈ zero |

## Honest read

**The affinity signal is essentially unused.** The policy isn't building or exploiting pairwise relationships — values stay at noise floor. Why this happened (most likely):

1. **Sparse events:** focal collaborates only 0.75 times/ep → barely any share/flank events to seed affinity
2. **Decay vs. event rate mismatch:** half-life ~700 steps but events fire \<1/ep → decay wins
3. **Confirms rubber-duck critique #1:** heuristic non-focals don't react to affinity, so the focal has no behavioral consequence to learn

Marginal gains (+12% lifespan, +21% repro) are real but not from emergent allegiance — more likely from the obs-channel addition giving the policy slightly more to look at, plus the betrayal penalty discouraging some friendly-fire. **The "sect" concept didn't emerge** in this run.

## Suggested next move

The cheap "implement and pray" path didn't pan out. Real options:

- **Make heuristic non-focals condition on affinity** (share more with positive-affinity, retaliate harder against negative) — gives the focal a feedback loop to learn from. ~1-day change.
- **Multi-agent training (CTDE/MAPPO):** the proper architectural fix; bidirectional learning. Multi-week.
- **Force more interaction events:** smaller maps, denser agent spawning, more sharing pressure → more affinity samples per episode.

Your call on direction.

*Looking at the performance metrics comparing the cluster-spawn approach to v19 on uniform spawn, I'm seeing some interesting trade-offs: lifespan dropped significantly by 22%, but collaborative interactions jumped up 47%, and reproductions decreased by 25%, while affinity remains negligible. The cluster-spawn strategy seems to be cutting episodes short but encouraging more cooperation before that happens.

The policy trained on uniform spawning is struggling in this new distribution, which explains why the non-collaborative metrics took a hit—it's operating in less-explored territory. But the fact that cluster-spawn recovers collaboration count above even v18's baseline is a strong signal that retraining is the right move. I'm going to launch lstm_v19b training now and check the configuration first.*

<sub>⏱️ 2602m 27s</sub>

### 💬 Copilot

Both are real and explain why v19 affinity telemetry came back near-zero. Let me give you concrete numbers from the code.

---

## 1. Decay vs. event-rate mismatch

**The constants:**
- `AFFINITY_DECAY_PER_STEP = 0.999` → half-life ≈ 693 steps
- `AFFINITY_NORM = 5.0` (so raw value 5.0 → normalised 1.0)
- `AFFINITY_BETRAY_THRESHOLD = 0.5` → need normalised ≥ 0.5 = raw ≥ **2.5**
- A single SHARE bumps the recipient→sharer affinity by `+1.0` raw (the strongest event)

**Bedrock arithmetic:** to get one pair from 0 → above the betrayal threshold (raw 2.5), you need **at least 3 SHARE events between the same ordered pair, with no decay in between**. Eval observed `ep_focal_max_affinity ≈ 0.04` — so across an entire 2000-step episode, the maximum normalised affinity any focal accumulated toward any other agent was 0.04 (raw ≈ 0.2). That's roughly ~0.5 events worth, decayed.

**Why the rates don't match:**
- v19 eval: `ep_focal_collaborate_count ≈ 0.75/episode`, food-shares are even rarer. Call it ~1 share-event per episode focal-side.
- One event raises a pair's raw affinity by ~1.0 (so ~0.2 normalised after norm). Then decay starts eating it: after 100 steps, ≈ 90% remains; after 700 steps, ≈ 50% remains.
- For the affinity *signal* to ever cross 0.5 normalised — i.e. for "betrayal" or "mutual-share bonus" to even be possible — the **same ordered pair** must accumulate 3+ positive events within ~few-hundred steps. With ~1 event/episode total across all 90 pairs (10 agents × 9 partners), the expected events per specific pair per episode is ~1/90 ≈ 0.01.
- **The decay is faster than the event arrival rate by two orders of magnitude.** So affinity stays glued near 0.

This is *visible* in the eval log: max affinity 0.04, betrayals 0, friendly-flanks 0. The state variable exists and updates correctly — but it never reaches a level where any reward path actually fires. PPO sees a constant-zero feature and a constant-zero reward bonus, so it has nothing to optimise on.

**Two ways out (both needed):**
1. **Slower decay** (e.g. 0.9995 → half-life ~1400 steps), so a single positive event lingers long enough for the next one to compound.
2. **More event sources**, so the per-pair event rate goes up. Right now we record affinity on: SHARE, ATTACK, STEAL, FLANK. We do *not* record on: COLLABORATE (group formation), proximity over time, joint GATHER on the same tile, joint kill of a monster, joint stash deposit.

---

## 2. Non-focals don't react to affinity

Look at the architecture honestly:

- The PPO policy controls only **one agent** per environment — `self._focal_idx`. It receives obs, picks an action, gets a reward.
- The other 9 agents are **scripted heuristics** (`_heuristic_step` and friends in `multi_env.py`). They run on hand-coded rules: "if hungry and food adjacent → EAT", "if low health → REST", "if stash adjacent and inventory \> 0 → DEPOSIT", etc.

**The affinity matrix updates for everyone** (events between any two agents are recorded). But:

- The PPO focal *can* read its own affinity row from the observation (we added the channel) and *could* learn "I have positive history with this neighbour, share with them more / don't attack them".
- Non-focals **never look at the affinity matrix.** Their decision tree has no `if self._affinity(self_idx, other_idx) \> X:` branches anywhere. They share with whoever happens to be adjacent, attack whoever happens to be hostile, etc.

**Concrete consequence:** A "coalition" requires multi-party reciprocity. Agent A shares with B → A→B affinity rises. For B to *reciprocate* (share back, defend A, refrain from attacking A), B's behaviour must depend on B→A affinity. But B is a heuristic and B→A affinity is data B never reads. So there is no closed feedback loop. Even if PPO's focal becomes a perfect ally-builder, its allies are emotionless robots that won't return the favour.

In a real multi-agent learner (CTDE / MAPPO / parameter-shared PPO with one network per agent), all agents would read affinity and the loop would close. Right now we have 1 learning agent + 9 fixed scripts.

**Two practical fixes (cheap-to-expensive):**
- **Cheap (this week):** Add a few `if self._affinity(self_idx, other_idx) \> X` branches into the heuristics — e.g. "share food preferentially with positive-affinity neighbours", "don't attack positive-affinity neighbours unless hostile", "follow the highest-affinity neighbour with small probability". This makes non-focals at least *consistent* with affinity, even if they don't learn it.
- **Expensive (multi-week):** Move to parameter-shared PPO where every agent uses the same policy network at decision time (one agent's experience trains the shared net). This is the proper fix and unlocks real coalition learning.

---

**Recommended sequence for next attempt** (since you said add more events):
1. Lower `AFFINITY_DECAY_PER_STEP` to 0.9995 (cheap, one constant)
2. Add affinity events on: COLLABORATE (both ways, like FLANK), joint deposit at same stash (small +), persistent proximity bonus (e.g. `+0.05` per step within radius 2 — but capped to avoid blowup)
3. Add 2–3 affinity branches into the heuristic share/attack code so non-focals at least respect affinity asymmetrically
4. Then retrain v19c

Want me to implement steps 1–3 next?

For persistent proximity, I'd sweep agents every K steps and apply small bonds between any pair within Chebyshev radius 2, though I need to find the right place in the step structure and check if existing tests would break. Now I'm working through the affinity magnitudes: COLLABORATE at 0.4, JOINT_KILL at 0.6 for the strong shared victory effect, and PROXIMITY at 0.02 per sweep. The proximity value is tiny but accumulates over time—with a half-life of 693 steps and decay of 0.999, I need to calculate the equilibrium to ensure proximity bonds actually push affinity into a useful range rather than just decaying away.

Settling on a simpler approach: apply proximity bonds every 5 steps with a delta of 0.015 to any pair within radius 2, which keeps the per-step cost trivial at O(N²). I'll add the new constants for collaboration, joint kill, and proximity parameters, create a helper function to apply proximity bonds called from the main step, and hook into the existing collaborate and attack paths for the other bond types.

def test_collaborate_records_symmetric_affinity_bond() -> None:
    """Successful _try_collaborate (group formed) records +AFFINITY_COLLAB_BOTH both ways."""

    other_idx = (focal_idx + 1) % env._n_agents

    focal.position = (5, 5)
    other.position = (5, 6)

def test_proximity_bonds_accrue_for_adjacent_agents() -> None:
    """Co-located agents accumulate proximity bond on every PROXIMITY_TICK_EVERY-th step."""
    from murimsim.rl.multi_env import (
        AFFINITY_PROXIMITY_PER_STEP, AFFINITY_PROXIMITY_TICK_EVERY,
        AFFINITY_PROXIMITY_RADIUS, AFFINITY_NORM,
    )
    env = CombatEnv(config=_load_cfg(), n_agents=4, seed=0)
    env.reset(seed=0)
    # Place agents 0 and 1 adjacent; agents 2 and 3 far away.
    env._agents[0].position = (5, 5)
    env._agents[1].position = (5, 5 + AFFINITY_PROXIMITY_RADIUS)  # within radius
    env._agents[2].position = (20, 20)
    env._agents[3].position = (20, 22)
    # Force tick alignment, then call directly.
    env._ep_step_count = AFFINITY_PROXIMITY_TICK_EVERY
    pre = env._affinity(0, 1)
    env._apply_proximity_bonds()
    post = env._affinity(0, 1)
    expected_delta = AFFINITY_PROXIMITY_PER_STEP / AFFINITY_NORM
    assert abs((post - pre) - expected_delta) < 1e-6
    # Should be symmetric.
    assert abs(env._affinity(1, 0) - post) < 1e-6
    # Far agents (0 and 2) should not have any bond.
    assert env._affinity(0, 2) == 0.0
